preconditions: The journey has three steps: session, details and confirmation.

assistiveTechnologyTests.procedure: Complete the journey and listen for the announcement or information under test.

title: Step indicator is hidden from assistive technology
description: Every page shows a visible Step n of 3 indicator, but the alpha path marks it aria-hidden. Sighted users know where they are in the journey; screen-reader users are not told.

relatedElements.note: The beta path exposes the same visible indicator without aria-hidden.

expectedBehaviour: The current step is available to assistive technology on every page of a multi-step journey.
actualBehaviour: The step text is visible but carries aria-hidden=true, so it is absent from the accessibility tree.
userImpact: Screen-reader users cannot tell where they are or how much of the booking remains.

wcag.note: Information conveyed visually is removed from the programmatic structure.

detection.note: The rendered text looks correct; only the accessibility tree shows the omission.

observed.note: Page-level axe run with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and best-practice. No violation was reported in the default state; the control on the same page or path also passes.

manualTests: Open step 2 with a screen reader running and listen for the step position.

assertions: The step indicator has aria-hidden=true while remaining visible.
tests: tests/journey-defects.spec.js: hides the step indicator from assistive technology on the alpha path

reviewStatus.note: A Playwright regression test preserves the defective journey or widget behaviour and its control. That is automated reproduction, not a manual or assistive-technology observation.
